+# Finite Graph Languages as Symbolic Systems
+
+## Abstract
+
+Finite graph languages are compact, closed and invariant under the one-sided shift.
+
+Let V be a finite vertex type with a discrete topology, and let edge be any directed relation on V. The one-sided graph language consists of the vertex sequences following edge at every consecutive pair. The compactness and shift-invariance results do not require right-totality. These are standard facts about finite graph presentations; no literature novelty is claimed.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The natural adjacency matrix).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.adjacency`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.adjacency` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+adjacency(edge) is the V by V matrix over the natural numbers whose entry at (i,j) is 1 when edge(i,j) holds and 0 otherwise. This module defines the matrix but does not yet prove a formula relating its powers to realized prefix counts.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Every vertex has an outgoing edge).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.RightTotal`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.RightTotal` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+RightTotal(edge) means that for every v there exists w with edge(v,w). A private helper uses this condition to extend each nonempty finite edge path to an infinite path.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The graph language with vertex labels).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.edgeLanguage`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.edgeLanguage` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+edgeLanguage(edge) specializes FiniteObservationSofic.graphLanguage to the identity vertex labelling. Thus its elements are exactly the sequences w with edge(w(n),w(n+1)) for every natural n.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (The language is compact and closed).**
+
+$$\operatorname{IsCompact}\left(\operatorname{edgeLanguage}\left(\mathit{edge}\right)\right) \land \operatorname{IsClosed}\left(\operatorname{edgeLanguage}\left(\mathit{edge}\right)\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.edgeLanguage_isCompact_isClosed` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Each consecutive-edge constraint is closed because the finite vertex space is discrete. Their intersection is closed in the compact product V^N, hence compact. The identity-labelled language is its continuous image, and compact subsets of this Hausdorff product are closed. The conclusion includes empty languages and graphs with dead vertices.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Dropping the first vertex preserves the language).**
+
+$$\operatorname{MapsTo}\left(\operatorname{shift}\left(1\right), \operatorname{edgeLanguage}\left(\mathit{edge}\right), \operatorname{edgeLanguage}\left(\mathit{edge}\right)\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy.edgeLanguage_shift_invariant` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Here shift(1) is SymbolicDynamics.FullShift.shift(1). If a path satisfies every consecutive-edge constraint, its tail does too. The theorem proves forward invariance under the one-step shift; it does not assert surjectivity of that shift or an entropy formula.
+
+## References
+

+# Primitive Gauss sum nonvanishing
+
+## Abstract
+
+Primitive Dirichlet Gauss sums are nonzero by finite Fourier injectivity.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Nonvanishing at every nonzero modulus).**
+
+$$\forall N:Nat, [\operatorname{NeZero}\left(N\right)] \forall chi:\operatorname{DirichletCharacter}\left(C, N\right), \operatorname{IsPrimitive}\left(chi\right) \implies \operatorname{gaussSum}\left(chi, \operatorname{stdAddChar}\left(N\right)\right) \neq 0$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/CharacterSums/PrimitiveGaussSum.primitive_gaussSum_ne_zero` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural modulus N with NeZero N and every primitive complex Dirichlet character chi modulo N, the standard additive-character Gauss sum is nonzero. The statement includes N=1 and composite moduli.
+
+If the Gauss sum vanished, Mathlib's primitive Fourier-transform formula would force the discrete Fourier transform of chi to vanish. Injectivity of ZMod.dft would then make chi identically zero, contradicting its value one at one. This is a supporting API lemma using the classical finite Fourier theory already in Mathlib, with no claim of new mathematical novelty.
+
+The intended consumer is nonzero normalization of the modular Dirichlet translation twist; its q-expansion coefficient law remains future work. The Reg candidate is kernel checked but sourceSelection is absent and declared_validated enrollment is not claimed. The remaining source-audit obligation is tracked at https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23614.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Arith/CharacterSums/PrimitiveGaussSum.primitive_gaussSum_ne_zero`

+# Dual-Coset Fock Modules by Invariant Restriction
+
+## Abstract
+
+Dual-coset Fock sectors inside an auxiliary even lattice.
+
+Let D be any finite-rank integral symmetric lattice with even diagonal, including rank zero. Let beta be any integral charge. E has Gram matrix [[G,beta],[beta^T,0]]. It may be singular or indefinite. Oscillators are complex multivariate polynomials indexed by Fin(rank(D)) times N, and V_D is their finite-support direct sum over integral charges. Rho renames old variables into E; its retraction kills the added variables. J_t sends single(n,P) to single((n,t),rho(P)); P_t extracts last charge t and applies that polynomial retraction. P_t J_t is identity. action(a) compresses the actual ambient Y_E(J0(a)) between J1 and P1. Truncation is inherited state by state; product compatibility is proved separately.
+
+Creation series commute with the explicit polynomial rename by the pinned PowerSeries map and substitution laws. Translation polynomials and their coefficient supports transport along the same injective rename. The new acting charge has last coordinate zero, so the added cocycle terms vanish while every original half-diagonal contribution remains. Old current derivatives commute with rename, and derivatives in the added variables vanish. The original minus-one product theorem gives canonical multiplication recursion, which extends both coefficient transports to the entire original state space.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (All original source products).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.source_transport`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.source_transport` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every original state a,b and integer m, J0((Y_D(a))_m b)=(Y_E(J0(a)))_m J0(b). No source-product compatibility is assumed. The auxiliary construction, coefficient transport and canonical polynomial multiplication recursion prove this identity.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (The original occurrence recipe).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.action_monomial`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.action_monomial` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every integral charge a and every finite oscillator exponent e, action(single(a,monomial(e,1))) is shiftedWord(a,occurrences_D(e)). The recursion uses the original occurrence list. It does not compare independently chosen occurrence lists in the two lattices.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Invariant all-state Fock realization).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.module_transport`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.module_transport` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every original state a, every module vector v and every integer m, J1((action(a))_m v)=(Y_E(J0(a)))_m J1(v). Thus every mode of every original input preserves this actual sector.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Vacuum action).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.module_vacuum`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.module_vacuum` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every D and beta, action(vacuum_D) is the identity field: its mode -1 is identity and every other integer mode is zero.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Input differentiation).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.module_input_derivative`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Sectors/LatticeDualCosetModule.module_input_derivative` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+

+/- GID: D5/S1/Dynamics/Symbolic/FiniteGraphEntropy
+   generality: G

+   mirror-E: none(waiver:evidence-not-specified-by-formal-manifest)

+   utility: none
+   digest: Finite graph languages are compact, closed and invariant under the one-sided shift. -/
+
+/- This module records the finite graph to symbolic-dynamics bridge.  The
+right-total hypothesis is explicit: without it, a finite vertex path can end
+at a dead vertex and need not be the prefix of an infinite graph path. -/
+
+import D5.S1.Dynamics.Shadowing.FiniteObservationSofic
+import D5.S1.Dynamics.Symbolic.PrefixGrowthEntropy
+import Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Basic
+import Mathlib.Topology.Compactness.Compact
+import Mathlib.Topology.Instances.Discrete
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open Classical
+
+open Set Function
+open scoped Topology
+open SymbolicDynamics
+open D5.S1.Dynamics.Shadowing
+
+namespace D5.S1.Dynamics.Symbolic.FiniteGraphEntropy
+
+universe u
+
+variable {V : Type u} [Fintype V] [TopologicalSpace V] [DiscreteTopology V]
+
+/-- The adjacency matrix of a finite directed graph, over the natural numbers. -/
+def adjacency (edge : V → V → Prop) : Matrix V V ℕ :=
+  fun i j => if edge i j then 1 else 0
+
+/-- Every vertex has an outgoing edge.  This is the finite extension condition
+needed when infinite graph paths are identified with all finite edge paths. -/
+def RightTotal (edge : V → V → Prop) : Prop :=
+  ∀ v, ∃ w, edge v w
+
+/-- The one-sided edge language presented by a directed graph. -/
+def edgeLanguage (edge : V → V → Prop) : Set (ℕ → V) :=
+  graphLanguage edge id
+
+private def pathSet (edge : V → V → Prop) : Set (ℕ → V) :=
+  {p | ∀ n, edge (p n) (p (n + 1))}
+
+private theorem edgeLanguage_eq_pathSet_image (edge : V → V → Prop) :
+    edgeLanguage edge = (fun p : ℕ → V => p) '' pathSet edge := by
+  ext w
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨p, hp, hl⟩
+    refine ⟨w, ?_, rfl⟩
+    intro n
+    simpa only [edgeLanguage, id_eq] using
+      (show edge (w n) (w (n + 1)) from by
+        rw [← hl n, ← hl (n + 1)]
+        exact hp n)
+  · rintro ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨p, hp, fun _ => rfl⟩
+
+private theorem isClosed_pathSet (edge : V → V → Prop) :
+    IsClosed (pathSet edge) := by
+  rw [show pathSet edge = ⋂ n : ℕ, {p : ℕ → V | edge (p n) (p (n + 1))} by
+    ext p
+    simp only [pathSet, mem_iInter, mem_setOf_eq]]
+  apply isClosed_iInter
+  intro n
+  have hrel : IsClosed {q : V × V | edge q.1 q.2} := isClosed_discrete _
+  have hcont : Continuous (fun p : ℕ → V => (p n, p (n + 1))) :=
+    (continuous_apply n).prodMk (continuous_apply (n + 1))
+  exact hrel.preimage hcont
+
+/-- A finite graph language is compact, hence closed, in the full shift. -/
+theorem edgeLanguage_isCompact_isClosed (edge : V → V → Prop) :
+    IsCompact (edgeLanguage edge) ∧ IsClosed (edgeLanguage edge) := by
+  have hpath : IsCompact (pathSet edge) :=
+    isCompact_univ.of_isClosed_subset (isClosed_pathSet edge) (subset_univ _)
+  have himage : IsCompact ((fun p : ℕ → V => p) '' pathSet edge) :=
+    hpath.image continuous_id
+  constructor
+  · rw [edgeLanguage_eq_pathSet_image edge]
+    exact himage
+  · rw [edgeLanguage_eq_pathSet_image edge]
+    exact himage.isClosed
+
+/-- Dropping the first symbol of an edge path is again an edge path. -/
+theorem edgeLanguage_shift_invariant (edge : V → V → Prop) :
+    MapsTo (FullShift.shift (1 : ℕ)) (edgeLanguage edge) (edgeLanguage edge) := by
+  intro w hw
+  rcases hw with ⟨p, hp, hl⟩
+  refine ⟨(fun n => p (n + 1)), ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro n
+    exact hp (n + 1)
+  · intro n
+    simpa only [FullShift.shift_apply, id_eq, Nat.add_comm] using hl (n + 1)
+
+/-- Under right-totality, every nonempty finite edge path can be extended to
+an infinite path. -/
+private theorem finite_path_extend (edge : V → V → Prop)
+    (ht : RightTotal edge) (n : ℕ) (p : Fin (n + 1) → V)
+    (hp : ∀ i : Fin n, edge (p i.castSucc) (p i.succ)) :
+    ∃ w : ℕ → V, (∀ i, edge (w i) (w (i + 1))) ∧
+      ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), w i.val = p i := by

+  · simp [neutralPolynomialMode, shiftedCurrentPolynomial, hm,
+      polynomialInjection, liftIndex]
+  · by_cases hz : m = 0
+    · simp [neutralPolynomialMode, shiftedCurrentPolynomial, hm, hz, unit_lift,
+        bilinear_lift, hu, map_smul]
+    · simp only [neutralPolynomialMode, shiftedCurrentPolynomial, hm, hz, ↓reduceIte,
+        LinearMap.smul_apply, LinearMap.sum_apply, map_smul, map_sum]
+      change (m : ℂ) • (∑ j : Fin (D.rank + 1),
+        ((auxiliary D β).G i.castSucc j : ℂ) •
+          pderiv (j, (m - 1).toNat) (polynomialInjection D β p)) =
+        (m : ℂ) • ∑ j : Fin D.rank, (D.G i j : ℂ) •
+          polynomialInjection D β (pderiv (j, (m - 1).toNat) p)
+      rw [Fin.sum_univ_castSucc]
+      simp only [gram_old, gram_star]
+      rw [star_derivative D β p (m - 1).toNat, smul_zero, add_zero]
+      congr 1
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro j hj
+      exact congrArg ((D.G i j : ℂ) • ·)
+        (pderiv_rename (liftIndex_injective D β) (j, (m - 1).toNat) p)
+
+private theorem current_single_lift (t : ℤ) (i : Fin D.rank) (n : Charge D)
+    (m : ℤ) (p : Oscillator D) :
+    neutralMode (auxiliary D β) i.castSucc m (injection D β t (Finsupp.single n p)) =
+      injection D β t (Finsupp.single n (shiftedCurrentPolynomial D β t i n m p)) := by
+  simp only [injection_single, neutralMode, Finsupp.lsum_single, LinearMap.comp_apply,
+    Finsupp.lsingle_apply, current_polynomial_lift]
+
+private theorem current_original_intertwines (i : Fin D.rank) :
+    Intertwines D β 0 (neutralField D i) (neutralField (auxiliary D β) i.castSucc) := by
+  intro m
+  have h : (injection D β 0).comp ((neutralField D i)[[m]]) =
+      ((neutralField (auxiliary D β) i.castSucc)[[m]]).comp (injection D β 0) := by
+    apply Finsupp.lhom_ext
+    intro n p
+    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LatticeSugawaraCurrents.neutralField_ncoeff]
+    rw [current_single_lift]
+    simp [neutralMode, neutralPolynomialMode, shiftedCurrentPolynomial]
+  exact fun v => congrArg (fun f : Carrier D →ₗ[ℂ] Carrier (auxiliary D β) => f v) h
+
+private theorem current_compressed_intertwines (t : ℤ) (i : Fin D.rank) :
+    Intertwines D β t (compress D β t (neutralField (auxiliary D β) i.castSucc))
+      (neutralField (auxiliary D β) i.castSucc) := by
+  intro m
+  have h : (injection D β t).comp
+      ((compress D β t (neutralField (auxiliary D β) i.castSucc))[[m]]) =
+      ((neutralField (auxiliary D β) i.castSucc)[[m]]).comp (injection D β t) := by
+    apply Finsupp.lhom_ext
+    intro n p
+    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, compress_modes,
+      LatticeSugawaraCurrents.neutralField_ncoeff]
+    rw [current_single_lift, retraction_injection]
+  exact fun v => congrArg (fun f : Carrier D →ₗ[ℂ] Carrier (auxiliary D β) => f v) h
+
+open private derivative_creation normal_right_identity
+  from D5.S3.VertexAlgebra.LatticeAllStateField
+
+private theorem variable_state_field (x : Index D) :
+    Y D (Finsupp.single (0 : Charge D) (X x)) =
+      dividedDerivative x.2 (neutralField D x.1) := by
+  rw [X, stateField_monomial]
+  simp only [occurrences, Finsupp.toMultiset_single, one_nsmul,
+    Multiset.toList_singleton, wordField]
+  rw [actual_zero, normal_right_identity]
+
+/-- Canonical multiplication recursion on the original polynomial, independent of list order. -/
+private theorem multiplication_recursion (x : Index D) (n : Charge D) (p : Oscillator D) :
+    Y D (Finsupp.single n (X x * p)) =
+      (normalMinusOne (dividedDerivative x.2 (neutralField D x.1))
+        (Y D (Finsupp.single n p))).1 := by
+  have h : ((Y D (Finsupp.single (0 : Charge D) (X x)))[[-1]])
+      (Finsupp.single n p) = Finsupp.single n (X x * p) := by
+    rw [variable_state_field]
+    exact derivative_creation D x n p
+  have hp := LatticeActualStateFieldCalculus.minus_one_product_field D
+    (Finsupp.single (0 : Charge D) (X x)) (Finsupp.single n p)
+  change Y D (((Y D _)[[-1]]) _) = _ at hp
+  rw [h, variable_state_field] at hp
+  exact hp
+
+private def ambientWord (a : Charge D) : List (Index D) →
+    VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier (auxiliary D β))
+  | [] => actualField (auxiliary D β) (liftCharge D β 0 a)
+  | x :: tail => (normalMinusOne
+      (dividedDerivative x.2 (neutralField (auxiliary D β) x.1.castSucc))
+      (ambientWord a tail)).1
+
+/-- The normal-product recipe uses exactly the original occurrence order. -/
+def shiftedWord (a : Charge D) : List (Index D) → VertexOperator ℂ (Carrier D)
+  | [] => compress D β 1 (actualField (auxiliary D β) (liftCharge D β 0 a))
+  | x :: tail => (normalMinusOne
+      (dividedDerivative x.2 (compress D β 1 (neutralField (auxiliary D β) x.1.castSucc)))
+      (shiftedWord a tail)).1
+
+private theorem ambientWord_realization (a : Charge D) (w : List (Index D)) :
+    Y (auxiliary D β)
+      (injection D β 0 (Finsupp.single a (w.map (fun x => (X x : Oscillator D))).prod)) =
+      ambientWord D β a w := by
+  induction w with
+  | nil =>
+    rw [List.map_nil, List.prod_nil, injection_single, map_one, stateField_ground]
+    rfl
+  | cons x tail ih =>
+    simp only [List.map_cons, List.prod_cons, injection_single, map_mul,
+      polynomialInjection, rename_X]
+    rw [multiplication_recursion]
+    have ih' := ih
+    rw [injection_single] at ih'
+    change Y (auxiliary D β) (Finsupp.single (liftCharge D β 0 a)
+      (rename (liftIndex D β) (tail.map (fun x => (X x : Oscillator D))).prod)) = _ at ih'
+    rw [ih']
+    rfl
+
+private theorem word_original_intertwines (a : Charge D) (w : List (Index D)) :
+    Intertwines D β 0 (wordField D a w) (ambientWord D β a w) := by
+  induction w with
+  | nil => exact ground_original_intertwines D β a
+  | cons x tail ih =>
+    exact normal_intertwines D β 0
+      (derivative_intertwines D β 0 (current_original_intertwines D β x.1) x.2) ih
+
+private theorem word_shifted_intertwines (a : Charge D) (w : List (Index D)) :
+    Intertwines D β 1 (shiftedWord D β a w) (ambientWord D β a w) := by
+  induction w with
+  | nil => exact ground_compressed_intertwines D β 1 a
+  | cons x tail ih =>
+    exact normal_intertwines D β 1
+      (derivative_intertwines D β 1 (current_compressed_intertwines D β 1 x.1) x.2) ih
+
+private theorem monomial_ambient (a : Charge D) (e : Index D →₀ ℕ) :
+    Y (auxiliary D β) (injection D β 0 (Finsupp.single a (monomial e 1))) =
+      ambientWord D β a (occurrences D e) := by
+  rw [← occurrences_product D e]
+  exact ambientWord_realization D β a _
+
+/-- Original products are transported on all original inputs and all integer modes. -/
+theorem source_transport (a b : Carrier D) (m : ℤ) :
+    injection D β 0 (((Y D a)[[m]]) b) =
+      ((Y (auxiliary D β) (injection D β 0 a))[[m]]) (injection D β 0 b) := by
+  have h : (injection D β 0).comp ((Y D a)[[m]]) =
+      ((Y (auxiliary D β) (injection D β 0 a))[[m]]).comp (injection D β 0) := by
+    have linearEquality :
+        (fun a : Carrier D => (injection D β 0).comp ((Y D a)[[m]])) =
+        (fun a : Carrier D =>
+          ((Y (auxiliary D β) (injection D β 0 a))[[m]]).comp (injection D β 0)) := by
+      funext a
+      induction a using Finsupp.induction_linear with
+      | zero => simp
+      | add a b ha hb => simp only [map_add, Pi.add_apply,
+          Pi.add_apply, LinearMap.comp_add, LinearMap.add_comp, ha, hb]
+      | single n p =>
+        induction p using MvPolynomial.induction_on' with
+        | add p q hp hq => simp only [map_add, Finsupp.single_add,
+            map_add, Pi.add_apply, LinearMap.comp_add, LinearMap.add_comp, hp, hq]
+        | monomial e c =>
+          have hc : monomial e c = c • (monomial e 1 : Oscillator D) := by
+            rw [smul_monomial]; simp only [smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
+          rw [hc, ← Finsupp.smul_single]
+          simp only [map_smul, Pi.smul_apply, Pi.smul_apply, LinearMap.comp_smul,
+            LinearMap.smul_comp, RingHom.id_apply]
+          congr 1
+          rw [stateField_monomial, monomial_ambient]
+          exact LinearMap.ext (word_original_intertwines D β n (occurrences D e) m)
+    exact congrFun linearEquality a
+  exact congrArg (fun f : Carrier D →ₗ[ℂ] Carrier (auxiliary D β) => f b) h
+
+/-- The full literal recipe agrees with compression on every original basis input. -/
+theorem action_monomial (a : Charge D) (e : Index D →₀ ℕ) :
+    action D β (Finsupp.single a (monomial e 1)) =
+      shiftedWord D β a (occurrences D e) := by
+  apply HVertexOperator.coeff_inj
+  funext k
+  apply LinearMap.ext
+  intro v
+  rw [VertexOperator.coeff_eq_ncoeff, VertexOperator.coeff_eq_ncoeff]
+  change ((compress D β 1 _)[[-k - 1]]) v = _
+  rw [compress_modes, monomial_ambient,
+    ← word_shifted_intertwines D β a (occurrences D e), retraction_injection]
+
+/-- The entire Fock sector is invariant under every original all-state field. -/
+theorem module_transport (a v : Carrier D) (m : ℤ) :
+    injection D β 1 (((action D β a)[[m]]) v) =
+      ((Y (auxiliary D β) (injection D β 0 a))[[m]]) (injection D β 1 v) := by
+  induction a using Finsupp.induction_linear with
+  | zero => simp
+  | add a b ha hb => simp only [map_add, Pi.add_apply,
+      LinearMap.add_apply, ha, hb]
+  | single n p =>
+    induction p using MvPolynomial.induction_on' with
+    | add p q hp hq => simp only [map_add, Finsupp.single_add,
+        map_add, Pi.add_apply, LinearMap.add_apply, hp, hq]
+    | monomial e c =>
+      have hc : monomial e c = c • (monomial e 1 : Oscillator D) := by
+            rw [smul_monomial]; simp only [smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
+      rw [hc, ← Finsupp.smul_single]
+      simp only [map_smul, Pi.smul_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply,
+        RingHom.id_apply]
+      congr 1
+      rw [action_monomial, monomial_ambient]
+      exact word_shifted_intertwines D β n (occurrences D e) m v
+
+private theorem injection_vacuum :
+    injection D β 0 (vacuum D) = vacuum (auxiliary D β) := by
+  have hz : liftCharge D β 0 0 = 0 := by
+    funext i
+    induction i using Fin.lastCases <;> simp [liftCharge]
+  simp [vacuum, injection_single, hz]
+
+theorem module_vacuum : action D β (vacuum D) = identityField := by
+  apply HVertexOperator.coeff_inj
+  funext k
+  apply LinearMap.ext
+  intro v
+  rw [VertexOperator.coeff_eq_ncoeff, VertexOperator.coeff_eq_ncoeff]
+  apply injection_injective D β 1
+  rw [module_transport, injection_vacuum, stateField_vacuum,
+    identity_modes, identity_modes]
+  split_ifs <;> simp
+
+private theorem derivation_lift (p : Oscillator D) :
+    oscillatorDerivation (auxiliary D β) (polynomialInjection D β p) =
+      polynomialInjection D β (oscillatorDerivation D p) := by
+  induction p using MvPolynomial.induction_on with
+  | C c => simp [polynomialInjection]
+  | add p q hp hq => simpa only [map_add] using congrArg₂ (· + ·) hp hq
+  | mul_X p x hp =>
+    simp only [map_mul, polynomialInjection, rename_X, Derivation.leibniz]
+    rw [show oscillatorDerivation (auxiliary D β) (rename (liftIndex D β) p) =
+      rename (liftIndex D β) (oscillatorDerivation D p) from hp]
+    simp [oscillatorDerivation, MvPolynomial.mkDerivation_X, liftIndex, map_smul]
+
+private theorem source_translation (a : Carrier D) :
+    injection D β 0 (translation D a) =
+      translation (auxiliary D β) (injection D β 0 a) := by
+  have h : (injection D β 0).comp (translation D) =
+      (translation (auxiliary D β)).comp (injection D β 0) := by
+    apply Finsupp.lhom_ext
+    intro n p
+    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, translation_single, injection_single]
+    congr 1
+    rw [map_add, map_mul, derivation_lift]
+    congr 2
+    change polynomialInjection D β (∑ i : Fin D.rank, (n i : ℂ) • X (i, 0)) =
+      ∑ i : Fin (D.rank + 1), (liftCharge D β 0 n i : ℂ) • X (i, 0)
+    rw [Fin.sum_univ_castSucc]
+    simp [liftCharge, map_sum, map_smul, polynomialInjection, liftIndex]
+  exact congrArg (fun f : Carrier D →ₗ[ℂ] Carrier (auxiliary D β) => f a) h
+
+/-- Differentiation is on the original input; no ambient translation is restricted to sector one. -/
+theorem module_input_derivative (a : Carrier D) (m : ℤ) :
+    ((action D β (translation D a))[[m]]) = -(m : ℂ) • ((action D β a)[[m - 1]]) := by
+  apply LinearMap.ext
+  intro v
+  apply injection_injective D β 1
+  rw [module_transport, source_translation,
+    LatticeActualStateDerivative.state_derivative_modes]
+  simp only [LinearMap.smul_apply, map_smul, module_transport]
+
+open StateFieldResidueReconstruction (integerBinomial)
+
+def moduleLeft (p q r : ℤ) (a b v : Carrier D) (i : ℕ) : Carrier D :=
+  integerBinomial p i • ((action D β (((Y D a)[[r + i]]) b))[[p + q - i]]) v
+
+def moduleFirst (p q r : ℤ) (a b v : Carrier D) (i : ℕ) : Carrier D :=
+  (((-1 : ℂ)^i) * integerBinomial r i) •
+    ((action D β a)[[p + r - i]]) (((action D β b)[[q + i]]) v)
+
+def moduleSecond (p q r : ℤ) (a b v : Carrier D) (i : ℕ) : Carrier D :=
+  (((-1 : ℂ)^i) * integerBinomial r i) •
+    (StateFieldResidueReconstruction.epsilon r •
+      ((action D β b)[[q + r - i]]) (((action D β a)[[p + i]]) v))
+
+/-- Three separate supports and the literal all-integer original-product module identity. -/
+theorem module_borcherds (a b v : Carrier D) (p q r : ℤ) :
+    Function.HasFiniteSupport (moduleLeft D β p q r a b v) ∧
+    Function.HasFiniteSupport (moduleFirst D β p q r a b v) ∧
+    Function.HasFiniteSupport (moduleSecond D β p q r a b v) ∧
+    (∑ᶠ i : ℕ, moduleLeft D β p q r a b v i) =
+      ∑ᶠ i : ℕ, (((-1 : ℂ)^i) * integerBinomial r i) •
+        (((action D β a)[[p + r - i]]) (((action D β b)[[q + i]]) v) -
+          StateFieldResidueReconstruction.epsilon r •
+            ((action D β b)[[q + r - i]]) (((action D β a)[[p + i]]) v)) := by
+  classical
+  have hl (i : ℕ) : injection D β 1 (moduleLeft D β p q r a b v i) =
+      LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiLeftTerm (auxiliary D β) p q r
+        (injection D β 0 a) (injection D β 0 b) (injection D β 1 v) i := by
+    simp only [moduleLeft, map_smul, module_transport, source_transport,
+      LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiLeftTerm, LatticeAllStateReconstruction.mu]
+  have hf (i : ℕ) : injection D β 1 (moduleFirst D β p q r a b v i) =
+      LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiRightFirstTerm (auxiliary D β) p q r
+        (injection D β 0 a) (injection D β 0 b) (injection D β 1 v) i := by
+    simp only [moduleFirst, map_smul, module_transport,
+      LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiRightFirstTerm, LatticeAllStateReconstruction.mu]
+  have hs (i : ℕ) : injection D β 1 (moduleSecond D β p q r a b v i) =
+      LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiRightSecondTerm (auxiliary D β) p q r
+        (injection D β 0 a) (injection D β 0 b) (injection D β 1 v) i := by
+    simp only [moduleSecond, map_smul, module_transport,
+      LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiRightSecondTerm, LatticeAllStateReconstruction.mu]
+  obtain ⟨ambientL, ambientF, ambientS, ambientLaw⟩ :=
+    LatticeAllStateJacobi.borcherds (auxiliary D β)
+      (injection D β 0 a) (injection D β 0 b) (injection D β 1 v) p q r
+  have finitePullback (f : ℕ → Carrier D) (g : ℕ → Carrier (auxiliary D β))
+      (h : ∀ i, injection D β 1 (f i) = g i) (hg : Function.HasFiniteSupport g) :
+      Function.HasFiniteSupport f := by
+    apply hg.subset
+    intro i hi
+    change g i ≠ 0
+    rw [← h i, ← (injection D β 1).map_zero]
+    exact (injection_injective D β 1).ne hi
+  have finiteL := finitePullback _ _ hl ambientL
+  have finiteF := finitePullback _ _ hf ambientF
+  have finiteS := finitePullback _ _ hs ambientS
+  refine ⟨finiteL, finiteF, finiteS, ?_⟩
+  simp_rw [smul_sub]
+  change (∑ᶠ i : ℕ, moduleLeft D β p q r a b v i) =
+    ∑ᶠ i : ℕ, (moduleFirst D β p q r a b v i - moduleSecond D β p q r a b v i)
+  rw [finsum_sub_distrib finiteF finiteS]
+  apply injection_injective D β 1
+  rw [map_sub, map_finsum _ finiteL, map_finsum _ finiteF, map_finsum _ finiteS]
+  simp_rw [hl, hf, hs]
+  simp_rw [smul_sub] at ambientLaw
+  change (∑ᶠ i : ℕ, LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiLeftTerm (auxiliary D β) p q r
+      (injection D β 0 a) (injection D β 0 b) (injection D β 1 v) i) =
+    ∑ᶠ i : ℕ, (LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiRightFirstTerm (auxiliary D β) p q r
+      (injection D β 0 a) (injection D β 0 b) (injection D β 1 v) i -
+      LatticeAllStateJacobi.jacobiRightSecondTerm (auxiliary D β) p q r
+        (injection D β 0 a) (injection D β 0 b) (injection D β 1 v) i) at ambientLaw
+  rw [finsum_sub_distrib ambientF ambientS] at ambientLaw
+  exact ambientLaw
+
+/-- Rational pairing with a physical shift, before using the exact dual equation. -/
+def physicalPairing (a : Charge D) (μ : Fin D.rank → ℚ) : ℚ :=
+  ∑ i, ∑ j, (a i : ℚ) * (D.G i j : ℚ) * μ j
+
+/-- Exact duality identifies the rational physical pairing with the integral raw-power shift. -/
+theorem physical_pairing_integral (μ : Fin D.rank → ℚ)
+    (hDual : ∀ i, ∑ j, (D.G i j : ℚ) * μ j = (β i : ℚ)) (a : Charge D) :
+    physicalPairing D a μ = ((∑ i, a i * β i : ℤ) : ℚ) := by
+  simp only [physicalPairing, mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum, hDual]
+  push_cast
+  rfl
+
+/-- Concrete shifted ground action, on arbitrary oscillator polynomials. -/
+theorem action_ground_coefficients (a n : Charge D) (p : Oscillator D) (m : ℤ) :
+    ((action D β (Finsupp.single a (1 : Oscillator D)))[[m]]) (Finsupp.single n p) =
+      shiftedRawSingle D β 1 a (-m - 1) n p := by
+  change ((compress D β 1 (Y (auxiliary D β)
+    (injection D β 0 (Finsupp.single a (1 : Oscillator D)))))[[m]]) _ = _
+  rw [compress_modes, injection_single, map_one, stateField_ground, injection_single,
+    actualField, VertexOperator.ncoeff_of_coeff,
+    (actual_creation_coefficient_transport (auxiliary D β)
+      (liftCharge D β 0 a) (liftCharge D β 0 a)).2.2.1,
+    rawSingle_lift, retraction_injection]
+
+/-- The physical shift is genuinely rational; its action uses precisely its integral dual pairing. -/
+theorem physical_ground_action (μ : Fin D.rank → ℚ)
+    (hDual : ∀ i, ∑ j, (D.G i j : ℚ) * μ j = (β i : ℚ))
+    (a n : Charge D) (p : Oscillator D) (m : ℤ) :
+    physicalPairing D a μ = ((∑ i, a i * β i : ℤ) : ℚ) ∧
+    ((action D β (Finsupp.single a (1 : Oscillator D)))[[m]]) (Finsupp.single n p) =
+      epsilon D a n • Finsupp.single (a + n)
+        (∑ d ∈ (translatedPolynomial D a p).support,
+          (translatedPolynomial D a p).coeff d •
+            creationCoeff D a (-m - 1 - bilinear D a n - ∑ i, a i * β i + d)) := by
+  constructor
+  · exact physical_pairing_integral D β μ hDual a
+  · simpa only [shiftedRawSingle, one_mul] using action_ground_coefficients D β a n p m
+
+open private derivative_zero from D5.S3.VertexAlgebra.LatticeAllStateField
+
+/-- The actual source current has the literal shifted multiplication, charge and derivative modes. -/
+theorem action_current_coefficients (i : Fin D.rank) (n : Charge D)
+    (p : Oscillator D) (m : ℤ) :
+    ((action D β (Finsupp.single (0 : Charge D) (X (i, 0))))[[m]])
+        (Finsupp.single n p) =
+      Finsupp.single n (shiftedCurrentPolynomial D β 1 i n m p) := by
+  have hz : liftCharge D β 0 0 = 0 := by
+    funext j
+    induction j using Fin.lastCases <;> simp [liftCharge]
+  have hj : injection D β 0 (Finsupp.single (0 : Charge D) (X (i, 0))) =
+      Finsupp.single (0 : Charge (auxiliary D β)) (X (i.castSucc, 0)) := by
+    simp [injection_single, hz, polynomialInjection, liftIndex]
+  change ((compress D β 1 (Y (auxiliary D β) _))[[m]]) _ = _
+  rw [compress_modes, hj, variable_state_field, derivative_zero,
+    LatticeSugawaraCurrents.neutralField_ncoeff,
+    current_single_lift, retraction_injection]
+
+/-- Explicit finite charge and monomial extension of the literal nested field recipe. -/
+theorem action_expansion (v : Carrier D) :
+    action D β v = ∑ n ∈ v.support,
+      ∑ e ∈ ((basisMonomials (Index D) ℂ).repr (v n)).support,
+        ((basisMonomials (Index D) ℂ).repr (v n) e) •
+          shiftedWord D β n (occurrences D e) := by
+  have hsingle (n : Charge D) (p : Oscillator D) :
+      action D β (Finsupp.single n p) =
+        ∑ e ∈ ((basisMonomials (Index D) ℂ).repr p).support,
+          ((basisMonomials (Index D) ℂ).repr p e) •
+            shiftedWord D β n (occurrences D e) := by
+    conv_lhs => rw [← (basisMonomials (Index D) ℂ).linearCombination_repr p]
+    simp only [Finsupp.linearCombination_apply, Finsupp.sum, map_sum, map_smul,
+      Finsupp.single_finset_sum, ← Finsupp.smul_single,
+      coe_basisMonomials, action_monomial]
+  conv_lhs => rw [← Finsupp.sum_single v]
+  simp only [Finsupp.sum, map_sum, hsingle]
+
+private def fractionalLattice : LatticeData where
+  rank := 1
+  G _ _ := 2
+  symmetric _ _ := rfl
+  even_diagonal _ := ⟨1, by norm_num⟩
+
+/-- A genuinely fractional dual shift has a nonzero charge-changing mode. -/
+theorem fractional_dual_action :
+    (∀ i : Fin 1, ∑ j : Fin 1, (fractionalLattice.G i j : ℚ) * (1 / 2 : ℚ) = 1) ∧
+    (¬ ∃ n : Fin 1 → ℤ, ∀ i, (n i : ℚ) = (1 / 2 : ℚ)) ∧
+    ((action fractionalLattice (fun _ => 1)
+      (Finsupp.single (fun _ => -1) (1 : Oscillator fractionalLattice)))[[0]])
+      (Finsupp.single 0 (1 : Oscillator fractionalLattice)) =
+        Finsupp.single (fun _ => -1) (1 : Oscillator fractionalLattice) := by
+  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro i
+    change ∑ j : Fin 1, (2 : ℚ) * (1 / 2 : ℚ) = 1

+  · rintro ⟨n, hn⟩
+    have h : (2 : ℚ) * (n 0 : ℚ) = 1 := by linarith [hn 0]
+    have hi : (2 : ℤ) * n 0 = 1 := by exact_mod_cast h
+    omega
+  · rw [action_ground_coefficients]
+    have hs : (1 : Polynomial (Oscillator fractionalLattice)).support = {0} := by
+      simpa using Polynomial.support_C
+        (show (1 : Oscillator fractionalLattice) ≠ 0 from one_ne_zero)
+    norm_num [shiftedRawSingle, translatedPolynomial, bilinear, epsilon,
+      lowerCocycleExponent, paritySign, fractionalLattice, Fin.sum_univ_succ,
+      creationCoeff, exponential_constant, hs]
+
+end
+end D5.S3.VertexAlgebra.LatticeDualCosetModule

+**Theorem 37.2 (exact worst-case native Read minimum).** Under all
+the premises of Definition 37.1, for each integer $d>0$ the minimum
+uniform paid Read cap is exactly $2d$, both for complete-future
+readiness and for the joint task. In particular every correct such
+preparation has a lawful run requiring at least $2d$ Reads, even
+when it may use more updates, longer finite words and more finite local
+work. The same minimum cap holds with the independent zero-error
+randomization specified there. At $d=0$ the minimum is zero.
+
+Proof. First connect distinct streams to this native task, without
+assuming that a full incidence has already been acquired. Fix public
+inputs and, for the moment, a deterministic preparation. At any reached
+Read or return boundary, its entire accessible state is a function of
+the preceding binary reply word. Indeed its next local operations,
+literal and update choices are source-free functions of that state;
+updates return the same acknowledgement and stationary local operations
+reveal no source data. Induction on the actual finite operations gives
+the assertion. Thus the return cut $n$, output and retained evaluator
+are identical whenever the preceding reply word is identical. Physical
+differences in the unobserved source cannot be used as an extra branch
+of this accessible computation.
+
+Suppose two different streams $s,s'\in\mathscr R_d$ reached the
+same return reply word. They then return at the same $n$. Choose a
+birth $j$ at which their bits differ, and a finite $e\ge n$ with
+$v_e=F_e-1\ge j$. Such an $e$ exists. By Theorem 28.2 their
+actual physical supports at cut $e$ differ, since their first $v_e$
+birth bits differ. Choose one physical word in the symmetric difference
+of those two finite supports. The continuation consisting of $e-n$
+updates followed by a Read of that word has different replies on the
+two sources. This is one finite legal request at their common return
+cut. Their identical retained local evaluator would have to predict
+both values from the same accessible data and same request, which is
+impossible. Every distinct stream must therefore occupy a different
+return leaf. This argument also applies to the joint task, which
+contains the complete-future requirement. It does not require equality
+of the two current full incidences.
+
+The number of leaves required here is a classical supplier. Rainer A.
+Rueppel, [*Linear Complexity and Random Sequences*](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/3-540-39805-8_21.pdf),
+in *Advances in Cryptology — EUROCRYPT '85*, LNCS 219, pp. 167–188
+(1986), p. 174, equations (5)–(6), explicitly counts distinct binary
+**semi-infinite streams** of linear complexity at most $d$. For the
+present class his count is
+
+$$
+ D_d=|\mathscr R_d|
+     =1+\sum_{\ell=1}^{d}2^{2\ell-1}
+     =\frac{2\,4^d+1}{3}.
+ \tag{GPO.88}
+$$
+
+The added one is the zero stream. This imports the semi-infinite count,
+not a count of arbitrary length-$2d$ words, private registers or
+primitive periodic generators. Its parameter correspondence is as
+follows. An order-$r$ recurrence (GPO.75) is realized by the length-$r$
+register with state $(s_i,\ldots,s_{i+r-1})$, output $s_i$, and
+successor obtained by shifting and appending
+$\sum_{j<r}c_js_{i+j}$. Conversely that register gives (GPO.75)
+from index zero for every seed. A zero final feedback tap is legal;
+the all-zero row shifts an arbitrary seed out and hence includes finite
+transients. Taking the least possible register length identifies the
+linear complexity, and allowing any length at most $d$ gives exactly
+$\mathscr R_d$. Nonminimal presentations add no distinct streams.
+
+Equivalently, for $r>0$ put $A_s(x)=\sum_{i\ge0}s_ix^i$.
+Equation (GPO.75) is equivalent to
+
+$$
+ H(x)A_s(x)=P(x),\qquad
+ H(x)=1+\sum_{k=1}^{r}c_{r-k}x^k,
+ \qquad \deg P<r,\quad\deg H\le r.
+ \tag{GPO.89}
+$$
+
+The coefficients at degrees $i+r$ give the recurrence in the reverse
+direction; the coefficients below $r$ accommodate the arbitrary seed.
+Thus a polynomial $A_s$ is retained even when $H=1$: its transient
+numerator is not discarded. For a nonzero reduced $P/H$ with $H(0)=1$,
+the least permitted length is
+$\max\{\deg H,1+\deg P\}$, since every presentation has those
+two degree bounds after reduction and this length itself satisfies
+(GPO.89). The zero stream has length zero. This is the all-index and
+singular convention already used in Lemma 29.2 and its Massey
+§§II–IV and Reeds–Sloane §2 suppliers cited in §36. It verifies
+the domain match for (GPO.88); it does not restrict the count to
+invertible or purely periodic sources, or assert uniqueness of the
+actual private presentation.
+
+Now suppose a correct preparation has uniform Read cap $q$. Its
+return reply words form a prefix-free binary family of lengths at
+most $q$: after a return at a given reply word, source-free control
+cannot instead ask another Read on another run with that same word.
+The standard binary decision-tree capacity is at most $2^q$ leaves.
+For example, extending each leaf word to length $q$ gives disjoint
+nonempty sets of binary words, all lying in the $2^q$ length-$q$
+words. Arbitrarily many deterministic update or local operations
+between branches do not increase that capacity. The preceding native
+distinguishability argument and (GPO.88) force $D_d\le2^q$.
+For $d>0$,
+
+$$
+ 2^{2d-1}<\frac{2\,4^d+1}{3}\le2^{2d},
+ \qquad \lceil\log_2D_d\rceil=2d.
+ \tag{GPO.90}
+$$
+
+Consequently $q\ge2d$. These stream counts and binary-tree capacity
+are classical inputs; the source-specific deduction is that every
+full-future return of this native presence service needs that many
+distinct leaves. Query length, query choice, update timing and stored
+local computation do not supply further reply letters.
+
+For randomization, choose one lawful source realization per distinct
+stream, and fix the common public inputs. There are only $D_d$ such
+representatives. For each representative, correctness, finite return
+and the asserted cap hold on a measure-one set of independent tapes.
+The intersection of these finitely many sets has measure one. Any tape
+in it gives a deterministic preparation correct on all representatives,
+to which the same leaf bound applies. Hence a uniform almost-sure cap
+below $2d$ is impossible. If that cap is absent, the theorem makes no
+expected-cost assertion.
+
+For attainment use the actual source-blind preparation of Definition
+33.1 with $m=2d$. Theorem 33.2 obtains exactly the first $2d$
+birth bits by $2d$ paid binary presence Reads on that source, at cut
+$N(2d)$. Its finite synthesis in Lemma 29.2 determines the whole
+actual stream. Theorems 33.2 and 34.3 then provide the current
+labelled tree, $\mathcal Q_1$, and the installed finite local
+evaluator, with completed writes and retained binding as stipulated.
+Thus both tasks attain $Q=2d$. For $d=0$ the unique stream is
+already known; two actual updates reach a mature cut and local forward
+replacement supplies both tasks with no Read. Nonnegativity of $Q$
+proves the zero minimum. $\square$
+

+**Theorem 8.3 (odd clock and the sharp-interval crossing).** For all
+$k\ge1$, $u\in\mathcal T$, $n=\ell(u)$ and $x=\rho^{2k+1}u$, set
+$H=k+h_R(u)$. Then for every integer $s\ge1$,
+
+$$
+ P_x(R^{s-1}LL)=1\iff s\le H,
+ \qquad k\le H\le k+n-1.                        \tag{GPO.29}
+$$
+
+For $1\le j\le k$,
+
+$$
+ F_j^o(x)=\operatorname{sh}(\rho^{2(k-j)}u),
+ \qquad a_j^o(x)\ge2^{k-j}n.                     \tag{GPO.30}
+$$
+
+For $j\ge k$, $F_j^o(x)$ is a pruning of $\operatorname{sh}(u)$.
+Consequently, whenever $n\le B<2n$,
+
+$$
+ a_j^o(x)\le B\iff j\ge k\quad(j\ge1),
+ \qquad k=\min\{j\ge1:a_j^o(x)\le B\}.          \tag{GPO.31}
+$$
+
+Proof. Let $d=h_R(u)$, with rightmost original leaf label indicator
+$\eta$. At an original proper prefix $R^j$, $j<d$, the left child is
+an odd substituted nonempty tree and is a branch, so $R^jLL$ is present.
+For $j\ge d$, the suffix $R^{j-d}LL$ is evaluated inside
+$T_{2k+1+\eta}$. By (GPO.28) it is present exactly when
+$2k+1+\eta\ge2(j-d)+3$, equivalently $j<d+k$, for either value of
+$\eta$. This also covers suffixes that fail before their end. Taking
+$j=s-1$ gives (GPO.29); the original right path has at most $n-1$ edges.
+The clock here is this threshold $H$, not the right height of $x$,
+which by (GPO.25) can instead be $H+1$.
+
+For $j\le k$, write $w=\rho^{2(k-j)}u$. The actual equality
+$x=\rho^{2j+1}w$ lets Lemma 8.1 identify each pruning branch exactly
+with a branch of $w$. Starting at its root and recursing only at those
+branches proves the first equality in (GPO.30). The reused two-step
+composition inequality $\ell(\rho^2w)\ge2\ell(w)$, from ABT39.1,
+proves its lower bound.
+
+For $j\ge k$, every original leaf has zero branch test by (GPO.28).
+Starting at the original root, the traversal can therefore only retain
+original branches or stop earlier: it never descends below an original
+leaf. It is a pruning of the original shape and has at most $n$ leaves.
+For $j<k$, (GPO.30) has at least $2n>B$ leaves; at $j=k$ it has exactly
+$n$. These prove (GPO.31), including $n=1$. The proof does not assume
+monotonicity of $P_y(pR^jLL)$ on arbitrary full binary trees: that would
+be false without the substituted-source conditions. $\square$
+

+**Proposition 12.3 (time-only failure and the exact logical task).** Even
+with exact $n$, advice and known $\pi$, $T_o$ alone does not determine
+$u$ or its complete logical Read/applyRho behavior. For common source-free
+logical control and initialization, the equivalence of originals under
+all finite logical Read/applyRho/stop tests is exactly equality of $u$.
+The present target contains additional realization coordinates; this does
+not prove a minimal complete-memory encoding for every consumer.
+
+Proof. Choose any $n\in[A,B]$ and an $n$-leaf ordered shape. Its all-alpha
+and all-beta labellings at the same $k$ and orientation have equal counts,
+advice and $T_o$, but a logical Read at any original leaf address has
+different replies. More generally distinct finite ordered labelled trees
+have different four-valued replies at some literal address: descend through
+common branch roots until the first unequal node type or label. One Read
+and stop at that address distinguishes them. Equal originals have equal
+successor trees under every logical update and equal replies at every
+request; induction on the common logical controller gives equal choices
+and outputs. This proves exactly the stated task equivalence. The target's
+$k$ and $\pi$ also specify the authentic entrance and physical adapter;
+no lower bound here makes each such field necessary for every restricted
+consumer or every alternative memory representation. $\square$
+

+**Definition 27.1 (the alternative law-bearing source).** Retain the
+actual alpha initialization and the local service of Definitions 22.1
+and 24.1. In particular there is one actual mutable root, persistent
+physical child links named $a,b$, total paid literal presence
+$\operatorname{Read}(w)=\mathbf1_{w\in\operatorname{Pos}(X)}$ on
+all finite physical words, and only the legal serial localStep,
+applyRho and stop operations. Updates have their original common
+acknowledgement. Labels, writer, allocator, generator state, work and
+physical durations supply no additional observation. Actual root
+binding, grants, exclusive serialization, reliable completion and
+sufficient growing backing are premises of this service, with their
+own acquisition, installation and lifetime charges. No reset, cloned
+root, semantic-port sensor or read of a private generator is added.
+
+The additional source premise is the following actual actuator rule.
+Before update $t$, enumerate the beta leaves of the old physical tree
+by lexicographic order of their addresses, with $a<b$. These addresses
+are pairwise prefix-incomparable. The actuator really commits their
+births in that order; it updates each old leaf once and does not visit
+a newborn leaf during that update. At its $j$th birth since the alpha
+initialization it consumes the next bit $z_j$. If $z_j=1$, the new
+beta child is at $a$ and alpha at $b$; if $z_j=0$, their positions
+are reversed. Old branches and their links remain in place.
+Alpha-to-beta changes create no birth and consume no bit.
+
+The stream $z=(z_1,z_2,\ldots)$ is produced by an autonomous
+source-owned generator. Its initial state and parameters are fixed
+before the first birth. It advances exactly once per birth, with no
+other input, reset or change of source; presence queries, local
+computation, waiting and stopping do not advance it. The public
+chronological ordering is a condition on actual births, not merely a
+chosen sorting of semantic occurrences. Serial update remains the
+observer's action; no interrupt or observation inside it is provided.
+
+Two alternative authentic public promises will be considered
+separately in Definitions 29.1 and 30.1. Their respective bounds, this
+autonomy rule, the chronological rule and alignment to the first birth
+are supplied authentic premises. Coefficients, seed and private machine
+data remain initially unknown. None of those premises is certified by
+a finite observed prefix. This is a named alternative to arbitrary
+birth wiring, rather than an inference about the source of §§22–26.
+

+**定理 2.1（全规模嵌套族）。** 对每个整数 $n\ge7$，令
+
+$$
+E_n=\{0,3\}\cup[5,n+2]_{\mathbb Z},\qquad B_n=A_{E_n}.
+$$
+
+则 $B_n\subsetneq B_{n+1}$、$|B_n|=n$，并且
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+|B_nB_n|&=2n+2\le3n-4,\\
+|B_n+B_n|&=M_n-\left[n-1+(n-8)_++(n-9)_++(n-11)_+
+                  +\mathbf1_{n\ge8}+\mathbf1_{n\ge10}\right],\\
+|B_n+B_n|&\le |G_n+G_n|-2.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{2.1}
+$$
+

Debrecen **77** (2010)，261–276，[DOI:10.5486/PMD.2010.4683](https://doi.org/10.5486/PMD.2010.4683)，Theorem 2.3(1)–(3)；对角碰撞的唯一性见该文 Theorem 2.2，连续幂计数见 Theorem 1.1(5) 及 pp.275–276。以下在同一推导内给出所需的初等论证，并始终以 $n$ 表示实际元素数。
+
+由 $\rho^3=\rho+1$ 得
+
+$$
+\rho^4=\rho^2+\rho,\qquad \rho^5=\rho^2+\rho+1,\qquad
+\rho-1=\rho^{-4},\qquad \rho^2-1=\rho^{-1},\qquad \rho^3>2.
+$$
+
+整数方程 $\rho^u-\rho^v=1$ 的全部解为
+
+$$
+(u,v)\in\{(1,-4),(2,-1),(3,1),(5,4)\}.
+\tag{2.2}
+$$
+
+事实上 $u>v$ 且 $u>0$。若 $v<0$，则 $1<\rho^u<2<\rho^3$，所以 $u=1$ 或 $2$；利用上面的恒等式分别得到 $v=-4$ 或 $-1$。若 $v\ge0$，置 $k=u-v$，则 $0<\rho^k-1=\rho^{-v}\le1$，所以 $k=1$ 或 $2$；对应地得到 $(u,v)=(5,4)$ 或 $(3,1)$。反向代入验证这四个解。
+
+任意两个不同的无序指数对若满足 $\rho^i+\rho^j=\rho^k+\rho^\ell$，将各对内部排序并交换两对后，必有 $i<k\le\ell<j$：最小指数若相同则可消去而使两对相同；最小指数严格较小的一对必须有严格较大的最大指数。除以 $\rho^i$ 后，方程化为
+
+$$
+1+\rho^d=\rho^a+\rho^b,\qquad 1\le a\le b<d.
+$$
+
+置 $s=d-b$。因为
+
+$$
+\rho^s=1+\rho^{a-b}-\rho^{-b}<2<\rho^3,
+$$
+
+所以 $s=1$ 或 $2$。在 $s=1$ 时方程等价于 $\rho^a-\rho^{b-4}=1$；在 $s=2$ 时等价于 $\rho^a-\rho^{b-1}=1$。将 (2.2) 代入并保留 $1\le a\le b$，所得全部可能性为
+
+$$
+(d,a,b)=(4,2,3),\ (6,3,5),\ (7,5,5),\ (9,5,8).

+这些正是定义 1.2 的四个模板。此处包含负整数的原始指数，也包含重复加数。

+还须确保不同碰撞没有重复扣减同一个和。以无序指数对为顶点，把等和的不同顶点相连。四类边的两个端点内部指数差依次为

+7\leftrightarrow0,\qquad9\leftrightarrow3.
+$$

+### Proposition 1.1: source independence is not observed-party independence
+
+The product law implies
+
+\[
+I(\alpha:\beta:\gamma)=0,
+\]
+
+where the total correlation is
+
+\[
+I(\alpha:\beta:\gamma)
+=
+D\!\left(
+\mu_{\alpha\beta\gamma}
+\middle\|
+\mu_\alpha\otimes\mu_\beta\otimes\mu_\gamma
+\right).
+\]
+
+It does not imply \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) are independent. Alice and Bob share \(\gamma\), Alice and Charlie share \(\beta\), and Bob and Charlie share \(\alpha\). The observed outputs can therefore be strongly correlated even though the three sources are mutually independent.
+
+**Proof.** The first assertion is the defining product condition. The second follows because, for example, \(A\) and \(B\) are both functions of \(\gamma\), in addition to their other inputs. A common edge is enough to create output correlation. No common tripartite source is required. ∎

+## 7. What the current literature establishes
+
+The precise status is as follows.
+
+1. **Fritz.** A standard CHSH test can be embedded in the triangle by using two independent classical sources as effective input bits and one entangled source for the Bell pair. The obstruction is therefore inherited from ordinary Bell nonlocality. It is a valid triangle-nonlocal example, but it does not isolate the genuinely network-specific joint-measurement effect.

+2. **Renou et al. 2019.** The four-output family \(P_u\), generated by three entangled sources and a four-outcome joint measurement, is proven non-trilocal for
+   \[
+   u_{\max}^2<u^2<1,\qquad u_{\max}^2\approx0.785.
+   \]

+### Theorem 2.1 (joint finite comparison and limit)
+
+For every integer $r\geq2$, the model in Section 1 satisfies
+
+$$
+ \kappa_{2r+1}^2(y_r)-\kappa_{2r+1}^2(x_r)
+ =2\left[
+ \binom{2r}{r}^{\!2}
+ -\frac{\binom{4r}{2r}}{2r+1}-2
+ \right]>0,
+ \tag{2.2}
+$$
+
+and
+
+$$
+ H_{2r+2}(y_r)-H_{2r+2}(x_r)
+ =\frac{f(2r)+f(2)-2f(r+1)}{4(r+1)}>0.
+ \tag{2.3}
+$$
+
+Moreover,
+
+$$
+ \lim_{r\to\infty}
+ \bigl(H_{2r+2}(y_r)-H_{2r+2}(x_r)\bigr)=\frac12
+ \quad\text{bit}.
+ \tag{2.4}
+$$
+
+**Proof.**
+
+For the entropy calculation, we use the single-deletion run-length formula
+of Singhvi--Sabary--Bar-Lev--Yaakobi [2, 3]. If $x\in\Sigma_m$ has
+consecutive run lengths $a_1,\ldots,a_s$, with $\sum_i a_i=m$, it gives
+
+$$
+  H_{m+1}(x)=\log_2(2(m+1))
+  -\frac{1}{2(m+1)}\sum_{i=1}^{s}f(a_i+1).
+  \tag{2.5}
+$$
+
+To fix the normalization and index-embedding convention, there are
+$2(m+1)$ insertion pairs: an insertion position and an inserted bit. Inserting the bit equal to a run symbol into the $a_i+1$ positions of
+that run gives one supersequence of weight $a_i+1$. Every other insertion
+pair gives a supersequence of weight $1$; two different insertion pairs can
+coincide only in the preceding run-extension case. Hence, after expanding
+$-\sum_y p_x(y)\log_2p_x(y)$, the weight-one terms vanish and
+
+$$
+ H_{m+1}(x)=\log_2(2(m+1))
+ -\frac{1}{2(m+1)}\sum_i(a_i+1)\log_2(a_i+1).
+$$
+
+For the autocorrelation calculation, set
+
+$$
+ M_{ij}:=\binom{i+j-2}{i-1}\binom{2m-i-j}{m-i}
+ \qquad(1\leq i,j\leq m).
+$$
+
+The matrix $M$ is symmetric and every row has the same sum
+
+$$
+ S_m:=\sum_{j=1}^{m}M_{ij}=\binom{2m-1}{m-1}.
+ \tag{2.6}
+$$
+
+Indeed, with $k=j-1$, (2.6) is the finite Vandermonde identity
+
+$$
+ \sum_k\binom{(i-1)+k}{i-1}
+       \binom{(2m-i-1)-k}{m-i}
+ =\binom{2m-1}{m-1},
+$$
+
+where binomial coefficients outside their natural range are zero. This is
+the classical Vandermonde convolution: by the binomial series [4, Equation
+(26.3.4)], the left side is the coefficient of $t^{m-1}$ in
+
+$$
+ (1-t)^{-i}(1-t)^{-(m-i+1)}=(1-t)^{-(m+1)},
+$$
+
+whose coefficient is $\binom{2m-1}{m-1}$.
+
+If $P$ and $N$ are respectively the zero and one positions of a binary
+word, define $W(P,N)=\sum_{i\in P,\,j\in N}M_{ij}$. Since the ordered
+cross terms occur twice and all other entries are equal-letter terms,
+
+$$
+  \kappa_m^2(w)=mS_m-2W(P,N).
+  \tag{2.7}
+$$
+
+Write $B_r=\binom{2r}{r}$ and $C_r=\binom{4r}{2r}$. In this matrix,
+the endpoint entries are
+
+$$
+ M_{11}=M_{mm}=C_r,
+ \qquad M_{1m}=M_{m1}=1,
+ \qquad M_{r+1,r+1}=B_r^2,
+ \tag{2.8}
+$$
+
+and $S_m=\binom{4r+1}{2r}=\frac{4r+1}{2r+1}C_r$. The zero positions of
+$x_r$ are $1,m$, so (2.6) and (2.8) give
+
+$$
+ W(x_r)=2(S_m-C_r-1).
+ \tag{2.9}
+$$
+
+The one position of $y_r$ is $r+1$, so its zero positions are all other
+positions and
+
+$$
+ W(y_r)=S_m-B_r^2.
+ \tag{2.10}
+$$
+
+Subtracting (2.7), then using (2.9)--(2.10), yields
+
+$$
+ \kappa_m^2(y_r)-\kappa_m^2(x_r)
+ =2\bigl(B_r^2+S_m-2C_r-2\bigr)
+ =2\left(B_r^2-\frac{C_r}{2r+1}-2\right),
+$$
+
+which is (2.2) as an identity.
+
+It remains to prove its strict sign. Let
+
+$$
+ Q_r:=\frac{C_r}{2r+1},
+ \qquad D_r:=B_r^2-Q_r.
+$$
+
+The factorial formula for binomial coefficients [4, Equation (26.3.1)]
+gives
+
+$$
+ B_{r+1}^2=\alpha_rB_r^2,
+ \quad \alpha_r=\frac{4(2r+1)^2}{(r+1)^2},
+$$
+
+$$
+ Q_{r+1}=\beta_rQ_r,
+ \quad \beta_r=
+ \frac{2(4r+1)(4r+3)}{(r+1)(2r+3)}.
+$$
+
+For $r\geq1$,
+
+$$
+ \alpha_r-\beta_r
+ =\frac{2(8r^2+9r+3)}{(r+1)^2(2r+3)}>0,
+ \qquad \alpha_r>1.
+$$
+
+Thus $D_{r+1}=\alpha_rD_r+(\alpha_r-\beta_r)Q_r>D_r$ whenever
+$D_r>0$. At the required endpoint $D_2=\binom42^2-\binom84/5=22$,
+so $D_r>2$ for every $r\geq2$. This proves the strict inequality in
+(2.2).
+
+The run lengths of $x_r$ are $1,2r-1,1$, while those of $y_r$ are
+$r,1,r$. Applying (2.5) gives
+
+$$
+ \begin{aligned}
+ H_{2r+2}(y_r)-H_{2r+2}(x_r)
+ &=\frac{(2r)\log_2(2r)+2-2(r+1)\log_2(r+1)}{4(r+1)}\\
+ &=\frac{f(2r)+f(2)-2f(r+1)}{4(r+1)}.
+ \end{aligned}
+$$
+
+Because $f''(t)=1/(t\ln2)>0$, strict midpoint convexity at the distinct
+points $2$ and $2r$ gives $f(2)+f(2r)>2f(r+1)$ for $r>1$, proving
+(2.3). Finally, elementary logarithm rules rewrite this difference as
+
+$$
+ \frac12-
+ \frac{\log_2 r}{2(r+1)}-
+ \frac12\log_2\left(1+\frac1r\right).
+ \tag{2.11}
+$$
+
+Both subtracted terms tend to zero, proving (2.4). $\square$
+
+At $r=1$, the two words in (2.1) coincide: $x_1=y_1=010$. Both
+differences in (2.2)--(2.3) are then $0$, so the strict range $r\geq2$
+is exact for this family. The theorem concerns this joint family only; it
+does not assert a general finite $\kappa^2$-ordering, a result for more
+than one deletion, or a deletion-channel capacity statement. It also leaves
+unchanged the fixed-$m$, $n\to\infty$ asymptotic minimization regime studied
+in arXiv:1807.11609v1.

+\tag{12.3}
+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+C_{\rm src}\ge
+\max\left\{0,\frac{\log m}{2}-h(\varepsilon)
+                         -\varepsilon\log(m-1)\right\}.
+\tag{12.4}
+$$
+
+For $m=1$ the output is constant and the conclusion is simply $C_{\rm src}\ge0$; no $\log(m-1)$ expression is used.
+
+*Proof.* Use Fano's finite-alphabet inequality in nats, with $B$ itself as an estimator of $A$, and separately with $C$ as an estimator of $A$. If their actual error probabilities are $e_B,e_C$, the classical inequality gives
+
+$$
+H(A\mid B)\le h(e_B)+e_B\log(m-1),\qquad
+H(A\mid C)\le h(e_C)+e_C\log(m-1).
+\tag{12.5}
+$$
+

+H(A\mid B)=H(E_B\mid B)+H(A\mid E_B,B)
+\le h(e_B)+e_B\log(m-1).

+$$

+ \#\{X_n\text{ over this }S\}&=2^c,\\
+ \#\{S\text{ attained at }n\}&=2^{F_n-1},\\
+ \#\{X_n\text{ attained at }n\}&=2^{F_{n+1}-1}.

+$\ell(T_m)=F_{m+1}$. Every branch therefore has a unique rank
+$m\ge2$, determined by its leaf count, since these counts are
+strictly increasing from rank one onward. At rank $m\ge3$ its
+child leaf counts $F_m,F_{m-1}$ are unequal. The physical shape
+therefore identifies which child has which rank. Rank two is the
+sole exception: both children are leaves, one beta and one alpha.

+births. Hence there are $2^{F_{n+1}-1}$ labelled trees, without

+## 3. What “three-dimensional” means in the network interface
+
+The triangle incidence matrix has three edge columns and three party rows. Each party sees exactly two columns:
+
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|ccc}
+ & \alpha & \beta & \gamma\\
+\hline
+A&0&1&1\\
+B&1&0&1\\
+C&1&1&0
+\end{array}.
+\tag{3.1}
+\]
+
+This is a three-edge incidence geometry. It is not a coordinate chart for physical space.
+
+The FIB three-axis interface starts with a supplied real positive-definite \(g\), a nonzero trilinear form \(T\), and full simultaneous \(SO(V,g)\)-invariance. Under those hypotheses, the invariant tensor calculation gives
+
+\[
+T=0\quad(d\ne3),\qquad
+T=c\,\operatorname{vol}_g\quad(d=3).
+\tag{3.2}
+\]
+
+The associated bilinear response is \(B=c\,\times_g\). The result is a conditional representation theorem for a response interface. It does not follow from the existence of three sources, three parties, or a cycle.
+
+The correct combined interpretation is:
+
+- the network contributes three independent edge slots and two-edge local access;
+- the FIB quotient contributes a three-coordinate observable carrier;
+- the hidden \(\kappa\)-fiber records information lost by that quotient;
+- a full triangle-local model is a lift of the observed carrier that must preserve the product law on the three edges and every unconnected-source invariance;
+- an inflation proof is a finite lifted obstruction to such a global lift.
+
+This is the same distinction used elsewhere in the project between a local projection and a future-complete boundary. A valid projection can be geometrically closed and still fail to have a compatible hidden lift.
+

+### Proposition 1.2: why source-product mixtures need a separate lift
+
+Let \(P\) and \(P'\) be triangle-local with source products \(\mu_\alpha\mu_\beta\mu_\gamma\) and \(\mu'_\alpha\mu'_\beta\mu'_\gamma\). The mixture
+
+\[
+tP+(1-t)P'
+\tag{1.3}
+\]
+
+has the evident hidden representation
+
+\[
+t\,\mu_\alpha\mu_\beta\mu_\gamma
++
+(1-t)\,\mu'_\alpha\mu'_\beta\mu'_\gamma.
+\]
+
+The evident implementation uses one shared selector \(S\) to choose between the two entire models. Giving \(S\) to every edge generally correlates the augmented edge variables \((S,\alpha)\), \((S,\beta)\), and \((S,\gamma)\), violating their independence. Independent selectors preserve a product law but generally introduce cross terms instead of the desired two-term mixture. Therefore this construction does not establish triangle locality of the mixture; a different local representation might still exist.
+
+This is the precise point where the Bell-hyperplane intuition breaks. In an ordinary Bell scenario, convex mixtures can be implemented by a shared hidden selector because one source already connects the relevant parties. In the triangle scenario, a selector shared by all three edge sources is an additional common ancestor and changes the causal graph.

+## 0. Main statement
+
+A triangle network has three source edges and three party vertices:
+
+\[
+E=\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\},\qquad V=\{A,B,C\},
+\]
+\[
+I(A)=\{\beta,\gamma\},\qquad I(B)=\{\gamma,\alpha\},\qquad I(C)=\{\alpha,\beta\}.
+\]
+
+The word three has three different meanings that must be kept separate.
+
+1. There are three independent edge sources.
+2. A finite observation may have three retained coordinates, such as the Auric FIB quotient \((X,Y,Z)\).
+3. A nonzero fully \(SO(3)\)-invariant alternating response is three-dimensional under the explicit hypotheses of the stable-relation volume.
+
+Only the third item is a dimension theorem, and it is conditional on a supplied real positive-definite metric, a nonzero trilinear response, and full simultaneous \(SO(V,g)\)-invariance. Source count alone does not imply a spatial dimension.
+
+The useful common object is therefore a **fibered incidence geometry**:
+
+\[
+\text{independent edge measure}
+\longrightarrow
+\text{two-edge local response}
+\longrightarrow
+\text{observed quotient}
+\]
+
+with a hidden gluing fiber above the quotient. In the five-mode Auric FIB carrier, the quotient is \((X,Y,Z)\), while \(\kappa\) is the residual two-edge coupling. In the triangle network, source independence is a separate product constraint on \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\). The two constraints are related by the incidence map, but they are not the same equation.
+

+**Theorem 11.1 (all-address odd-offset Read macro).** Fix $k\ge1$, any
+logical current tree $t\in\mathcal T$, and actual register
+$y=\rho^{2k+1}t$. For a nonroot address $p=ad$, $d\in\{L,R\}$, set
+
+$$
+ G_k^o(p)=aR^kLL.                                  \tag{GPO.36}
+$$
+
+In addition to (GPO.26), this is a total paid presence query. Its bit
+$g$ is one exactly when $p$ was present in $t$. The complete actual table
+is
+
+| Logical reply $r_t(p)$ | $g$ for nonroot $p$ | $b$ | $c$ |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| absent | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ |
+| alpha | $1$ | $0$ | $0$ |
+| beta | $1$ | $1$ | $0$ |
+| branch | $1$ | $1$ | $1$ |
+
+The following adaptive macro returns precisely $r_t(p)$ without updating
+$y$: first Read $B_k^o(p)$; if $b=1$, Read $C_k^o(p)$ and return beta
+or branch according as $c=0$ or $1$. If $b=0$ at the root, return alpha.
+If $b=0$ at a nonroot, Read $G_k^o(p)$ and return absent or alpha
+according as $g=0$ or $1$. Only paid presence bits enter this control.
+For $D_p=|p|+k+1$ its exact path costs are
+
+| Logical request/reply | $Q_p$ | $W_p$ | $M_p$ |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| root alpha | $1$ | $D_p$ | $D_p$ |
+| beta or branch, any $p$ | $2$ | $2D_p+1$ | $D_p+1$ |
+| nonroot alpha or absent | $2$ | $2D_p$ | $D_p$ |

+## 5. Inflation as a discrete covering and obstruction
+
+Inflation replaces each source edge by several copies and each party by copies connected according to the incidence pattern. The resulting graph is a finite cover-like lift of the original causal incidence complex. A triangle-local model induces a distribution on the lifted parties with:
+
+- equal-copy symmetries;
+- marginal consistency whenever two lifted events descend to the same original event;
+- factorization or d-separation constraints for disjoint source copies;
+- the original \(P(a,b,c)\) as an appropriate marginal.
+
+The lifted feasible event vectors form a convex relaxation. The original triangle-local set remains non-convex because the source product structure is still imposed before the response contraction. This explains the apparently paradoxical division of labor:
+
+- the original local set is non-convex;
+- an inflation relaxation is a convex polytope or cone;
+- an infeasibility certificate is a linear separating cochain for the lifted relaxation;
+- a certificate must separate the required target from every lifted deterministic image, not merely be positive on those images.
+
+More precisely, let \(K\) map a lifted law to the coordinates constrained by inflation, and let \(T(P)\) be the target coordinates required by the observed distribution. Soundness must first establish that a triangle-local \(P\) admits a lifted probability law \(q\) with \(K(q)=T(P)\). A linear functional \(f\) certifies infeasibility when
+
+\[
+\left\langle f,K(\delta_\omega)-T(P)\right\rangle>0
+\quad\text{for every lifted deterministic event }\omega.
+\]
+
+Indeed, taking the convex combination with coefficients \(q(\omega)\) would give \(0>0\). Positivity of \(\langle f,K(\delta_\omega)\rangle\) alone is insufficient: the target value must also be compared. For rational maps and targets, clear their denominators by a common positive integer and verify the resulting strict integer inequalities. This is an exact separation certificate, not a floating-point numerical distance.
+
+The 2025 Gitton–Renner EJM result is the canonical example. The EJM distribution has four outcomes per party,
+
+\[
+P_{\mathrm{EJM}}(a,b,c)=
+\begin{cases}
+25/256,&a=b=c,\\
+5/256,&a,b,c\text{ all distinct},\\
+1/256,&\text{otherwise}.
+\end{cases}
+\tag{5.1}
+\]
+
+A symmetry-reduced inflation with source-copy size \((2,2,4)\), followed by a Frank–Wolfe search and an exact integer certificate, proves that this distribution is outside the classical triangle-local set. The proof is a global gluing obstruction in a lifted event space. It is not a Bell inequality on the original three-party table.
+
+This makes the geometry-to-network map precise: the EJM proof does not merely find a negative coordinate in the three-dimensional quotient. It shows that no globally consistent product-source lift exists after all copied-edge compatibility conditions are imposed.
+

+**Theorem 23.1 (acquired physical ancestor and exact semantic fiber).**
+In Definition 22.1's arbitrary-original domain, let $U$ be the authentic
+original written in its actual physical branch order. One common
+effective presence-only procedure acquires and retains $(U,k,n)$ with
+zero updates. For a fixed complete current physical presence service
+and the same authentic interval, the entire semantic target fiber is
+
+$$
+ \{(v,k,n):[v]=[U]\}.
+ \tag{GPO.64}
+$$
+
+Define the unordered-invariant integer $a$ by
+
+$$
+ a(\alpha)=a(\beta)=0,\qquad
+ a(\langle s,t\rangle)=a(s)+a(t)+\mathbf1_{[s]\ne[t]}.
+ \tag{GPO.65}
+$$
+
+There are exactly $2^{a(U)}$ different semantic originals in (GPO.64).
+The fiber is a singleton exactly for perfect monochromatic originals,
+including either single labelled leaf. On every nonsingleton fiber,
+uniform recovery of the original semantic Read/applyRho task from this
+service fails even with arbitrarily many adaptive forward updates.
+The positive acquisition and the negative semantic conclusion concern
+the same full realization class.
+
+Proof. First acquire the finite current physical shape $X$ by a stack
+traversal. Its root is known present. At each confirmed node $p$, pay
+Read$(pa)$; this bit classifies branch versus leaf in a full binary
+tree. Schedule $pa,pb$ only on a branch. Each actual node is visited
+once and stack exhaustion terminates without a size or height oracle.
+Now apply $D_{\rm loc}$, erase the decoded labels, and repeat until
+the first decoded leaf count is at most $B$.
+
+For decoding stage $j\le k$, Theorem 22.2 gives precisely the actual
+physical version of $\rho^{2(k-j)}u$. Its leaf count is at least
+$2^{k-j}n$, using ABT39.1's two-step growth. At every $j<k$ it is
+at least $2n\ge2A>B$, whereas at $j=k$ it is $n\le B$.
+Even the initial count exceeds $B$. Thus the first crossing is exactly
+$k$, no parse past the authentic original is attempted, and the
+returned labels and physical branch order are exactly $U$. All parsing,
+counting and comparisons use finite acquired strings and public advice.
+Actual retained writes make $(U,k,n)$ readable on this same run.
+
+Any alternative realization with the same complete physical presence
+service gives the same $X$, and this deterministic decoding/crossing
+gives the same $U,k,n$. Its semantic original is therefore in $[U]$.
+Conversely, fix any ordered $v$ with $[v]=[U]$. A rooted
+label-preserving unordered isomorphism assigns local frames at its old
+branches so its physical original is exactly $U$. Follow corresponding
+leaves through each actual update: matched alpha leaves become matched
+beta leaves; matched beta leaves create corresponding beta/alpha
+children. Choose their local birth frames to match the physical
+placements of the original realization. Old branches keep their
+frames. Induction realizes the same complete labelled physical tree
+at entrance, not just the same marginal shape, with semantic original
+$v$ and the same authentic $k,n$. This proves both directions of
+(GPO.64).
+
+Let $E(W)$ count ordered labelled representatives of an unordered
+class $W$. A leaf has $E=1$. A branch with distinct child classes
+$X,Y$ has $E=2E(X)E(Y)$, because their two physical positions are
+distinct choices. With equal child classes it has $E=E(X)^2$:
+every ordered pair of representatives occurs, and there is no
+additional exchange factor. Induction proves $E([U])=2^{a(U)}$.
+For $a(U)=0$, every branch has isomorphic children and both have
+zero $a$. Inductively they are perfect monochromatic trees of the
+same height and colour. This proves precisely the singleton
+classification, with its converse immediate from (GPO.65).
+
+For persistence of ambiguity, take any two different ordered originals
+in (GPO.64) with the matched labelled physical entrance trees just
+constructed, and common accessible initialization. After entrance choose
+the same physical rule, for example beta always placed at $a$, at every
+matched new birth in both realizations. This is a legal actual choice
+sequence; it needs no changing adversary or future oracle. Equal
+physical labelled trees then give equal physical presence replies and
+equal labelled successors under each update. Induction on the full
+accessible actions gives identical requests, acquired records, local
+control, acknowledgements, stopping and outputs for every finite
+adaptive controller. Even granting full future physical labels would
+leave this pair indistinguishable. The different semantic originals
+have different four-valued replies at some original semantic address,
+by the finite-tree distinction in Proposition 6.3. Hence no uniformly
+correct acquired adapter can serve all those original continuations.
+This is fiberwise identifiability; it does not deny that a constant
+program can name one source on a separately promised singleton input.
+$\square$

+**Lemma 29.2 (the classical finite separation in this domain).** Any
+two streams of $\mathscr R_d$ agreeing in their first $2d$ output
+bits agree at every index. From such a prefix there is a terminating
+finite algorithm producing a generator for the actual full stream.
+It need not recover its private coefficients, register or seed
+presentation.
+
+Proof. For a stream of order $r$, let $E$ be forward shift on
+one-sided sequences and put
+$p(E)=E^r-\sum_{j<r}c_jE^j$. The monic polynomial $p$
+annihilates that stream at every nonnegative index. If $q$ similarly
+annihilates the other stream of order $r'$, commuting shifts make
+$p(E)q(E)$ annihilate their difference. This polynomial is monic of
+degree $r+r'\le2d$. A sequence satisfying that homogeneous forward
+recurrence and having its first $r+r'$ entries zero has every entry
+zero, by induction. Agreement through $2d$ therefore suffices. This
+argument includes degree zero, zero trailing taps and singular shifts;
+it never runs the recurrence backwards.
+
+For an explicit algorithm when $d>0$, pad any order-$r$ annihilator
+to order $d$ by multiplication by $E^{d-r}$. Enumerate all $2^d$
+coefficient rows for a monic order-$d$ recurrence. Give each candidate
+the observed first $d$ bits as its initial seed, generate its first
+$2d$ bits, and retain the first candidate matching the observed word.
+At least the padded actual recurrence passes. Every passing candidate
+belongs to $\mathscr R_d$, so the separation just proved makes its
+entire output equal to the actual stream. A fixed enumeration makes
+the returned behavioral description canonical. At $d=0$ simply
+return the known zero generator. All operations are finite binary
+operations; no exact-real comparison or source oracle is involved.
+
+The separation and shift-register synthesis are classical suppliers,
+not new identification results. Massey, *Shift-Register Synthesis and
+BCH Decoding*, §II–III, explicitly permits a zero final tap and gives
+the $2L$ synthesis boundary; his §IV distinguishes finite transient
+numerator degree from denominator degree. Reeds–Sloane, §2 of
+*Shift-Register Synthesis (Modulo m)*, retains that finite-length
+convention in its broader ring setting. Here only the binary field
+and the all-index bounded class (GPO.75) are used. The direct monic
+argument verifies their applicability to the stated nonminimal and
+singular domain. $\square$
+

+\tag{2.9}

+\tag{2.11}

+\[
+d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p,p_*)
+=\frac12\|p-p_*\|_1
+=\frac{2|\Delta|}{r},
+\qquad
+\|p-p_*\|_1=\frac{4|\Delta|}{r}.
+\tag{2.12}

+### 5.1 A concrete three-dimensional EJM encoding
+
+There is an exact geometric encoding of the four EJM outcomes that makes the three-dimensional connection concrete without identifying the network with physical space. Let \(t_0,t_1,t_2,t_3\in\mathbb R^3\) be the unit vectors at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron, so
+
+\[
+t_i\cdot t_j=
+\begin{cases}
+1,&i=j,\\
+-1/3,&i\ne j.
+\end{cases}
+\]
+
+For an output triple \((a,b,c)\), put
+
+\[
+d_{ab}=t_a\cdot t_b,\quad
+d_{bc}=t_b\cdot t_c,\quad
+d_{ca}=t_c\cdot t_a,
+\]
+\[
+S=d_{ab}+d_{bc}+d_{ca},\qquad
+R=d_{ab}d_{bc}+d_{bc}d_{ca}+d_{ca}d_{ab}.
+\]
+
+Then the exact EJM table (5.1) is the symmetric Gram polynomial
+
+\[
+P_{\mathrm{EJM}}(a,b,c)=\frac{4+S+6R}{256}.
+\tag{5.2}
+\]
+
+The three equality patterns give
+
+\[
+\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
+\text{pattern}&S&R&(4+S+6R)/256\\
+\hline
+a=b=c&3&3&25/256\\
+\text{exactly two equal}&1/3&-5/9&1/256\\
+a,b,c\text{ all distinct}&-1&1/3&5/256.
+\end{array}
+\]
+
+Among the 64 ordered output triples, four are all equal, 36 have exactly two equal entries, and 24 are all distinct. Thus every entry is nonnegative and the total mass is
+
+\[
+\frac{4\cdot25+36\cdot1+24\cdot5}{256}=1.
+\]
+
+The Gram expression therefore specifies an exact rational probability law on the 64 output triples.
+
+This identity is an exact finite calculation. It is a genuine three-dimensional representation of the output symmetry because the four outcomes are encoded by a regular tetrahedron in \(\mathbb R^3\). It is not a proof that the causal sources are spatial axes.
+
+The term \(S\) is a sum of pairwise Gram interactions. The term \(R\) is the symmetric sum of pairwise products among the three edge-pair Gram entries, so it is a cycle-sensitive invariant that still respects the full permutation symmetry of \(a,b,c\). Equivalently,
+
+\[
+256P_{\mathrm{EJM}}
+=5-4(\delta_{ab}+\delta_{bc}+\delta_{ca})
++32\,\mathbf 1_{\{a=b=c\}}.
+\]
+
+The last form makes the three pattern weights transparent; the Gram form makes the regular-tetrahedron, three-dimensional realization transparent. The identification of \(R\) with a physical curvature or holonomy remains a conjectural interpretation. What is proved here is only the polynomial identity (5.2).
+
+The encoding also explains why a purely low-order quotient can be blind. A statistic that retains only one-party means or a single pairwise Gram average can preserve the same \((X,Y,Z)\) while losing the cycle-sensitive \(R\) sector. A global triangle-local test must keep enough lifted data to decide whether the pairwise Gram sectors and the symmetric cycle sector admit one common product-source realization.
+

+## 1. The exact triangle-local carrier
+
+Let \(\Omega_\alpha,\Omega_\beta,\Omega_\gamma\) be standard Borel source spaces with probability measures \(\mu_\alpha,\mu_\beta,\mu_\gamma\). A classical triangle model consists of the product measure
+
+\[
+\mu=\mu_\alpha\otimes\mu_\beta\otimes\mu_\gamma
+\]
+
+and three stochastic response kernels
+
+\[
+A(a\mid\beta,\gamma),\qquad
+B(b\mid\gamma,\alpha),\qquad
+C(c\mid\alpha,\beta).
+\]
+
+For every output triple,
+
+\[
+P(a,b,c)=
+\int_{\Omega_\alpha\times\Omega_\beta\times\Omega_\gamma}
+A(a\mid\beta,\gamma)
+B(b\mid\gamma,\alpha)
+C(c\mid\alpha,\beta)\,d\mu.
+\tag{1.1}
+\]
+
+The triangle-local set \(\mathcal L_\triangle\) is the set of all finite-output distributions admitting (1.1). The response kernels may contain local private randomness. Such randomness can be represented by additional independent local seeds and absorbed into the kernels. It must not be replaced by a common selector shared by the three parties.
+
+For finite source alphabets the same object is a multilinear contraction. If the source probabilities are \(r_\alpha,r_\beta,r_\gamma\), then
+
+\[
+P(a,b,c)=
+\sum_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}
+r_\alpha r_\beta r_\gamma
+A_{a\mid\beta\gamma}
+B_{b\mid\gamma\alpha}
+C_{c\mid\alpha\beta}.
+\tag{1.2}
+\]
+
+This tensor form explains the geometry. The source point is a product point in the three source simplices. The response map is multilinear in the three edge measures. The image is generally non-convex.
+

+X=f_A(\beta,\gamma)=f_B(\gamma,\alpha)=f_C(\alpha,\beta)
+\quad\text{almost surely}.
+\tag{11.1}
+$$

+In particular,
+
+$$
+C_{\rm src}\ge\frac12H(X).
+\tag{11.2}
+$$
+
+Equality in (11.2) holds on this same realization if and only if both of the following conditions hold: the three source pairs are unconditionally independent, and for every $x$ with $p_x:=\mathbb P(X=x)>0$,
+
+$$
+\nu(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\mid X=x)
+=\nu_\alpha(\alpha\mid x)\nu_\beta(\beta\mid x)\nu_\gamma(\gamma\mid x)
+\quad\text{for all }\alpha,\beta,\gamma.
+\tag{11.3}
+$$

+Thus the conditional requirement is a threefold product on each positive output fiber, including its zero cells.

+*Proof.* First derive (11.1) from the stochastic kernels. For a source triple $s$ with $\nu(s)>0$, the conditional product of the three response vectors must give mass one to the output diagonal. +$$
+H(X\mid\alpha,\beta)=H(X\mid\alpha,\gamma)
+=H(X\mid\beta,\gamma)=H(X\mid\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=0.

+**证明。** 将 $E$ 写成 $\{x_1<\cdots<x_n\}$，令 $E_i=\{x_1,\ldots,x_i\}$。四种模板由其最大点唯一确定，相应的其余点距最大点的距离集合为
+
+$$
+L_4=\{1,2,4\},\quad L_6=\{1,3,6\},\quad
+L_7=\{2,7\},\quad L_9=\{1,4,9\}.
+$$
+
+记 $\mathcal L=\{L_4,L_6,L_7,L_9\}$，并定义以 $x_i$ 为最大点的副本数
+
+$$
+c_i=\sum_{L\in\mathcal L}\mathbf1_{\{x_i-a:a\in L\}\subseteq E_{i-1}}.
+$$
+
+取 $E_0=\varnothing$，则 $C(E_i)-C(E_{i-1})=c_i$、$0\le c_i\le4$。所以只需证明任意十点集满足 $C(E_{10})\le14$。
+
+对非空前缀 $E_i$ 定义距离状态
+
+$$
+S_i=\{a\in[0,8]_{\mathbb Z}:x_i-a\in E_i\},\qquad
+s_i=\sum_{a\in S_i}2^a.
+$$
+
+所有可能的状态属于
+
+$$
+\mathcal S=\{S\subseteq[0,8]_{\mathbb Z}:0\in S\};
+$$
+
+其编码 $s$ 恰为 $1,3,\ldots,511$，共 $256$ 个。相距当前最大点至少 $9$ 的旧点，与下一点相距至少 $10$；以后距离只会增加。由于模板的跨度至多为 $9$，这些旧点永远不能参与以后新增的副本，故丢弃它们没有损失。
+
+若下一相邻间隔为正整数 $g$，令
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+D(S,g)&=\{a+g:a\in S\},\\
+F(S,g)&=\{0\}\cup\bigl(D(S,g)\cap[1,8]_{\mathbb Z}\bigr),\\
+W(S,g)&=\sum_{L\in\mathcal L}\mathbf1_{L\subseteq D(S,g)}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{3.3}
+$$
+
+则 $S_{i+1}=F(S_i,g)$、$c_{i+1}=W(S_i,g)$。计数使用完整的 $D(S,g)$，随后才截取下一状态，因而距离恰为 $9$ 的所需点仍参与计数。若 $g\ge9$，则 $D(S,g)$ 中没有 $1$ 或 $2$，而每个 $L\in\mathcal L$ 都含 $1$ 或 $2$，故
+
+$$
+F(S,g)=\{0\},\qquad W(S,g)=0\qquad(g\ge9).
+\tag{3.4}
+$$
